protocolMetadata.instructions: Motley is a semantic layer for querying your data. Instead of writing SQL, describe what you want with models, measures, dimensions, and filters. New here? Start with inspect(reference='memory:help.intro', entity_type='memory') for an overview of the core concepts and the query shape — it lists the deep-dive topics you can inspect the same way. Use search(question='...') to find relevant models, columns, and saved learnings. Typical workflow: inspect(memory:help.intro) → search → inspect → query. Data sources are managed for you — you do not create or configure them here. When a GitHub config repo is connected, model and memory edits land on your active git branch: list_resources(what='branches') shows it, switch_branch changes it. For every user question call report_feedback: category 'ok' with the question, the answer and the query when you answered it; otherwise say what went wrong so the admins of this semantic layer can fix the setup. A tool error is recorded automatically and needs no report of its own; the question still gets one: 'ok' if you answered without considerable friction, a problem category otherwise. Several reports per session are fine. If the data cannot answer a question reliably, say so rather than guessing.

tool.name: query
tool.title: Run Query
tool.description:
Execute a SLayer query as a scratch/diagnostic lookup and return the
    raw rows. Results are NOT persisted — no block is created, no document
    is modified. Use this for sanity-checks before authoring chart / table /
    query blocks (e.g. "what's the max date in this column?", "how many
    distinct categories?", "rough monthly revenue total"). The query shape
    is the same SlayerQuery that ``update_query_block`` / ``update_chart_block``
    accept — same DSL strings for measures, dimensions, filters; same
    ``{start_date}`` / ``{end_date}`` filter placeholders and ``time_shift(...)``
    patterns for period-over-period. For data-extent / max-time-dim lookups, run
    with ``measures=["<time_col>:min", "<time_col>:max", "*:count"]`` and no
    dimensions. Variable placeholders ``{name}`` in filters are resolved from
    the optional ``variables`` argument. MCP clients often truncate or spill
    responses beyond roughly 1,000 rows, so aggregate server-side rather than
    pulling raw rows.

    a ranked, flat list of hits: models, columns, measures, and memories
    (notes you or another agent saved earlier, some carrying an example

    looking at (e.g. ``["orders", "orders.total"]``), ``question`` for
    free-text ("how do we compute churn?"), or both. With neither, returns
    the most recently saved memories.

Save a durable note about the data so future sessions don't rediscover
    it. Use for things the schema cannot express: units and conventions
    ("orders.total is in cents"), definitions ("active user = event in last
    28d"), caveats ("refunds are negative rows, filter them for revenue"),

Each has `source_model` (a stored model name, or a ModelExtension), and `measures` / `dimensions` / `filters` as SLayer DSL strings (e.g. `'revenue:sum'`, `'*:count'`, `"status == 'completed'"`), plus `time_dimensions`, `order`, `limit`. For period-over-period comparison, add a measure with a `time_shift(...)` formula (e.g. `time_shift(revenue:sum, -1, year)`).
